Ever
EV-er
adv.
Webster 1828 treats EVER as adverb: at any time (past or future); at all times / always / continually; forever, eternally, to perpetuity (with a looser sense of an indefinite period, as the servant in Exodus 21:6); ever and anon; in any degree; a word of emphasis; and in composition, always or to eternity. His own biblical illustrations include Ephesians 5:29, Psalm 111, 2 Timothy 3:7, Exodus 3:15, and forever and ever. This page fills the KJV-gap adverb of duration. Companion pages already treat eternal, forever, and everlasting.

Biblical Definition

Ever in Scripture is not a mood and not a brand. It names the duration of God’s name, the stability of Christ, and the counterfeit of endless study without truth. The psalmist will not let covenant be seasonal: he will ever be mindful of his covenant (Psa 111:5). The apostle will not let learning be a virtue by itself: Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth (2 Tim 3:7). The church will not get a new Jesus by decade: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever (Heb 13:8). The throne will not be leased: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever (Psa 45:6). The house of the LORD is not a weekend: I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever (Psa 23:6). The dictionary therefore keeps ever from becoming either open-ended process or a slogan for self-help permanence. It is the Bible’s way of saying: always — as the Lord is, not as the age feels.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines EVER as at any time; at all times / always; forever / to perpetuity (sometimes loosely, for an indefinite period); ever and anon; in any degree; and as a word of emphasis. He illustrates from Ephesians 5:29, Psalm 111, 2 Timothy 3:7, and Exodus 3:15.

expand to see more

EV'ER, adverb At any time; at any period or point of time, past or future. Have you ever seen the city of Paris, or shall you ever see it?

No man ever yet hated his own flesh. Ephesians 5:29.

1. At all times; always; continually.

He will ever be mindful of his covenant. Psalms 111:5.

Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. 2 Timothy 3:7.

2. Forever, eternally; to perpetuity; during everlasting continuance.

This is my name forever. Exodus 3:15.

In a more lax sense, this word signifies continually, for an indefinite period.

His master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him forever. Exodus 21:6.

These words are sometimes repeated, for the sake of emphasis; forever and ever or forever and forever.

3. ever and anon, at one time and another; now and then.

4. In any degree. No man is ever the richer or happier for injustice.

Ever in composition signifies always or continually, without intermission, or to eternity.

Key Scripture

Psalm 111:5 — "He hath given meat unto them that fear him: he will ever be mindful of his covenant."

2 Timothy 3:7 — "Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth."

Hebrews 13:8 — "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever."

Psalm 45:6 — "Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre."

Psalm 23:6 — "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever."

Modern Corruption

Ever is corrupted when the throne is treated as temporary, when ever learning is baptized as humility, and when for ever is emptied into a feeling of permanence without the living Christ.

expand to see more

The first corruption is process-God. Psalm 45:6 is for ever and ever; Hebrews 13:8 is the same Christ yesterday, today, and for ever. Open theism and every reduced Jesus keep the adverb and drop the throne. The recovery is the unchangeable Son, not a deity still becoming.

The second corruption is 2 Timothy 3:7 as a compliment. Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth is indictment. Credential culture and endless deconstruction treat non-arrival as sophistication. The dictionary will not. Learning that will not come to the truth is not humility; it is unbelief with a library card.

The third corruption is forever-as-brand. Therapeutic religion hears Psalm 23:6 as a spa: dwell in a mood for ever. The line is the house of the LORD, and Psalm 111:5 is a God who is ever mindful of His covenant. Permanence belongs to the Name, not to the self.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: at any time / always / forever. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew olam (H5769) at Psalm 111:5 and Psalm 45:6 (first ever); Hebrew ad (H5703) at Psalm 45:6 (second ever); Hebrew orek (H753) at Psalm 23:6; Greek pantote (G3842) at 2 Timothy 3:7; Greek aion (G165) at Hebrews 13:8. Exodus 3:15 carries no Strong’s tag on ever in this cache; this page does not mint one.

expand to see more

Hebrew olam (H5769) — ever, everlasting (Psa 111:5; Psa 45:6 first ever); Hebrew ad (H5703) — perpetuity (Psa 45:6 second ever).

Hebrew orek (H753) — length (Psa 23:6, for ever as length, not a minted olam on that line).

Greek pantote (G3842) — ever, at all times (2 Tim 3:7); Greek aion (G165) — age, forever (Heb 13:8).

Exodus 3:15 is KJV-verified as Webster’s illustration (this is my name for ever); the cache does not tag ever with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.

Usage

"The LORD is ever mindful of His covenant (Psa 111:5); His throne is for ever and ever (Psa 45:6)."

"Ever learning without the truth is not humility (2 Tim 3:7)."

"Christ is the same yesterday, today, and for ever (Heb 13:8); the saint dwells in the house of the LORD for ever (Psa 23:6)."
